prompt.context: Your company runs a chain of movie theatres (think General Cinema) and is considering opening a movie theater in Rittenhouse Square. Your boss wants to meet with you shortly and wants an estimate of the number of seats the theater should have.
prompt.question: What are the considerations regarding the market you would take into account and what is the number of seats you would recommend? Note: the question is not whether or not they should open a movie theatre.

clarifying_info.q: What type of theater is this?
clarifying_info.a: It is a mainstream theater — not art house or similar.

clarifying_info.q: How many screens will the theater have?
clarifying_info.a: Four screens. The interviewer ended up asking for the number of seats on a per-screen basis.

framework: Size the addressable population: identify Philadelphians interested in this mainstream theater
Filter by proximity: consider distance/catchment area around Rittenhouse Square
Assess competitive landscape: existing theaters, substitutes (streaming, other entertainment)
Segment the customer base: demographics such as age and income level
Estimate demand frequency: how many potential patrons would visit per week
Determine supply constraints: number of screens (4), shows per day/week per screen
Calculate seats per screen: total weekly demand ÷ total weekly show slots
Add a buffer for volatility: account for peak-demand shows (weekends, blockbusters)

questions.prompt: Walk through how you would size the population of potential patrons for this theater.
questions.guidance: Candidate should start with the Philadelphia metro population (~1.5M city, ~5M metro), narrow to the catchment area around Rittenhouse Square (dense urban neighborhood), apply demographic filters (age, income level appropriate for mainstream cinema), and exclude segments unlikely to attend (very young children, elderly with mobility issues, low-income households if ticket price is a barrier). Should also account for competition from nearby theaters.

questions.prompt: Given your estimate of potential patrons, how would you calculate the number of seats per screen?
questions.guidance: Strong answers build the calculation in clear steps: (1) Estimate weekly visits from the catchment population (e.g., what fraction goes to the movies each week), (2) Divide by the number of shows per week per screen (e.g., 3 shows/day × 7 days = 21 shows/screen/week, × 4 screens = 84 total show slots), (3) Derive average occupancy per show = total weekly attendance ÷ total show slots, (4) That average occupancy becomes the baseline seat count per screen. Candidate should note this is an average and recommend adding a buffer (e.g., 10–20%) to handle high-demand shows without turning away customers.

math.setup: Illustrative example — adjust assumptions as reasoned: Philadelphia catchment population ≈ 200,000 residents within walking/short transit distance; ~5% go to movies in a given week = 10,000 weekly visits to this theater (assuming one dominant competitor, so split demand); 4 screens × 3 shows/day × 7 days = 84 shows/week total; seats per show = 10,000 ÷ 84 ≈ 119 seats/show
steps: Add ~20% buffer for peak demand: 119 × 1.2 ≈ 143 seats per screen
math.answer: ~120–150 seats per screen (exact answer depends on assumed catchment size and visit frequency)

brainstorming.prompt: What market considerations would affect the viability and seat sizing for this theater?

categories.name: Demand-side factors
ideas: Catchment population size and density around Rittenhouse Square
Age and income demographics of the neighborhood
Frequency of movie-going behavior in the target segment
Preference for mainstream vs. art-house films

categories.name: Competitive landscape
ideas: Number and proximity of existing movie theaters in Philadelphia
Presence of streaming/home entertainment as substitutes
Other entertainment options in Rittenhouse Square area (restaurants, bars, live venues)

categories.name: Supply/operational factors
ideas: Show schedule: shows per day, days per week
Peak vs. off-peak demand variation (weekends, holidays, blockbuster releases)
Seat utilization targets and break-even occupancy rate

categories.name: Location-specific factors
ideas: Foot traffic and transit accessibility at Rittenhouse Square
Zoning and space constraints affecting maximum theater size

recommendation: Recommend approximately 120–150 seats per screen based on estimated weekly demand of ~10,000 visits divided across 84 weekly show slots, with a buffer for peak-demand volatility
Four screens × ~135 seats = ~540 total seats for the theater
risks: Catchment population estimate may be too high if competition is intense or if the neighborhood skews toward older/wealthier demographics with lower movie-going frequency
Streaming and home entertainment continue to erode theatrical attendance, which could make the theater oversized over time
Seasonal and blockbuster-driven demand spikes could still exceed even a buffered seat count
next_steps: Conduct primary research on actual foot traffic and demographics around Rittenhouse Square
Survey competitive theater utilization rates in Philadelphia
Model break-even occupancy to validate seat count against projected ticket revenue and fixed costs
